=== 2. GAZA - NO APPROVED-SOURCE OVERNIGHT DEVELOPMENT FOUND ===
The only genuinely NEW Gaza development found for 27 Sep is a letter from Israeli Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich and National Missions Minister Orit Strock to Netanyahu demanding Israel reject the Board of Peace's new Gaza plan. It is carried ONLY by The Jerusalem Post (https://www.jpost.com/israel-news/article-909898, published 27 September 2026 18:33/21:33), Israel Hayom, JNS, The Yeshiva World and teleSUR - NONE of which are on the approved-source list. Times of Israel has an equivalent story only from 3 August 2026 about the earlier 15-point roadmap, which is a DIFFERENT, older letter. THEREFORE: DO NOT PUBLISH the Smotrich letter. It is single-sourced to non-approved outlets.
Reported JPost content, for context only (NOT publishable): the ministers said the BoP proposal is "completely contrary to the understandings that were reached between you and the US administration and the Board of Peace"; they said a cabinet decision authorised only 200 ISF soldiers, "not 500, and certainly not 5,000".

Approved-source Gaza material available is all from 23-27 Sep and was already used in the 27 Sep evening brief (Al Jazeera on UNRWA exclusion, Saunders and Qassem quotes). Board of Peace six-month framework figures that ARE approved-source-backed via Al Jazeera 27 Sep: $2.4bn/66 projects; reconstruction needs $71.5bn; at least 1,451 Palestinians killed and 4,953 wounded since the October 2025 ceasefire began (Gaza Ministry of Health); more than half of hospitals and clinics non-functional; under 1.5% of cropland accessible and undamaged; nearly 84% of the population, more than 1.76 million people, in displacement sites or inadequate shelter (UN).

=== 3. OSINT CLAIMS OF IRGC MISSILE AND MINE ATTACKS - NOT CORROBORATED ===
NO approved source, and no UKMTO or CENTCOM product, reports a new IRGC missile or mine attack in the Strait of Hormuz on 27 or 28 September 2026.
- Most recent retrievable UKMTO warnings: 140-26, 141-26, 142-26, ALL dated 21 September 2026.
- Most recent retrievable UKMTO/JMIC advisory note: Update 099, dated 24 September 2026.
- Most recent retrievable UKMTO VRA overview: filename-dated 25 September 2026.
- Al Jazeera (27 Sep) reports explosions HEARD near Qeshm Island per Iranian media and says "Iranian authorities did not confirm any attacks in the Strait of Hormuz that day". That was already published in the 27 Sep evening brief.
- CNBC-TV18 (28 Sep, NOT an approved outlet) relays that "the Fars news agency reported that Iranian forces had targeted ships using unauthorised routes" - Fars is not approved and this is uncorroborated.
CONCLUSION: the OSINT aggregator claim remains UNCORROBORATED for a third time. Do not publish.

=== 4. MOLDOVA - FABRICATION TRAP, DISCARDED ===
A search result from next-edition.com (https://next-edition.com/articles/world-moldova-s-pro-eu-party-wins-parliamentary-election-despite-russian-interference-2026-09-27) claimed Moldova's PAS won a parliamentary election on Sunday 27 September 2026. The page is self-described as written "By AI Correspondent - Predicted for September 27, 2026". Moldova's parliamentary election was held 28 September 2025; results were validated by its Constitutional Court and reported by Moldpres and IPN. NPR's coverage of it is dated 29 September 2025. DISCARDED as fabricated. Do not publish.

=== 6. SOUTH KOREA / UKRAINE POW ROW - APPROVED SOURCE NOT SECURED ===
South Korea's presidential office demanded an explanation and apology from Ukraine over the disclosure of the transfer of two North Korean POWs; spokesman Seong Ghi-hong quoted saying the office "expresses strong regret over Ukraine's unilateral disclosure and its subsequent false announcement that there had not been a non-disclosure agreement" (statement released Sunday 27 Sep). The story is Reuters-derived but was retrieved only via The Times of India (Sep 28, 2026, 07:38 IST) and India Today (Sep 28, 2026 03:52 IST), both BANNED sources. A Reuters, AP or AFP original was NOT secured. DO NOT PUBLISH until an approved original is found.
